title: Merget: Merge queue for AI coding agents on GitHub
excerpt: Merget is a semantic merge queue for GitHub. It resolves merge conflicts between pull requests from parallel coding agents and lands them through your checks.
content_html:
Every merge into main multiplies your dev team’s workload.

Each pull request that lands moves main. Every open PR behind it can now conflict or fail CI, and each one is rebased, resolved and rechecked on its own, then again after the next merge.

Git can’t see every conflict.

One pull request renames a function. Another adds a call to its old name. Git merges both cleanly. Every branch passes alone. Main doesn’t.

Every PR wastes tokens and hours across your fleet of agents.

Each agent resolves the same conflicts and CI failures on its own branch. The more pull requests are open, the more of that work is repeated.

1 / 3

PRs from different agents conflict twice as often as PRs from the same agent.

In a replay study, cross-agent pull request pairs hit textual conflicts at about twice the rate of same-agent pairs. Those are only the conflicts Git can see.

Merget reads the code under every open PR, plans the queue and resolves the conflicts in parallel.

01 / Code graph

Read the code under every open PR.

Deep static analysis maps where each name is defined and who calls it across open pull requests. These connections form the foundation for finding conflicts, planning the queue and resolving them.

02 / Data and control flow

Find the conflicts Git misses.

Data and control flow reveal how changes in one pull request affect another. Merget uses that map to detect semantic conflicts that Git merges cleanly, alongside the textual conflicts Git reports.

03 / PR graph

Plan the queue. Resolve in parallel.

The PR graph shows which pull requests can land together and which must go in order. Merget resolves their conflicts in parallel: known shapes directly, and harder cases with coding agents. Every fix lands through your required checks and reviews.

1 / 3

See how it works

Clear the merge queue in minutes, not hours.

28.9 sto plan a queue of 40 mergesFlask, 40 workers

5.9 minto work through a 24-branch batch, against 11.5 min for agents merging one at a timeFlask batch 2, median

7 → 2agent sessions on the same batch with the one-call resolversame branch outcomes

$0.018modeled cost to resolve one conflicted file223 of 223 files resolved

See the benchmarks

Worktrees keep your agents apart. Merget resolves what collides when they merge.

Worktrees stop agents overwriting each other while they work, but their pull requests still conflict at merge time. GitHub’s merge queue removes a conflicting pull request for you to fix. Merget resolves it in queue order, with the pull requests ahead in view. What it cannot resolve safely comes back to a person.

Once their pull requests conflict, someone has to resolve them.

Compare GitHub merge queue alternatives

Merge queues, merge conflicts and coding agents.

What is Merget?

Merget is a semantic merge queue for GitHub, built for teams running AI coding agents in parallel. It finds conflicts between open pull requests, resolves them in queue order, and lands the result through your required checks and reviews. See how it works.

What is a semantic merge queue?

A semantic merge queue is a merge queue that finds and resolves conflicts in what code means, not only in its text, before pull requests land. For example, one pull request renames a function while another adds a call to its old name. Read the definition and example.

Does GitHub’s merge queue resolve merge conflicts?

No. GitHub’s merge queue removes a pull request that conflicts with the base branch or fails required checks, and the author fixes it and queues again. Merget works on the conflict in queue order instead. How GitHub’s merge queue works.

Do I need GitHub’s merge queue to use Merget?

No. Merget runs its own queue and manages its own landing order. No label, comment or enqueue command is needed, and branch protection is optional. It works with public and private repositories on GitHub.com, for organizations and personal accounts. Read the setup guide.

What are some alternatives to GitHub’s merge queue?

Merget, Mergify, Graphite, Trunk and Aviator are alternatives to GitHub’s merge queue. They differ most in what happens when pull requests conflict: Merget resolves the conflict in queue order, where most queues remove the pull request. Compare the alternatives.

How do I stop merge conflicts between parallel Claude Code agents in git worktrees?

Worktrees stop agents from overwriting each other’s files, but their branches still conflict when they merge. Keep each agent’s pull request small, then let a merge queue order and reconcile them: Merget resolves the conflicts between open pull requests in queue order, so no agent rebases by hand. Read the worktree guide.

Why do pull requests pass CI and still break main?

Because each pull request is tested against the main it branched from, not against the pull requests landing beside it. One renames a function while another adds a call to its old name; Git merges both cleanly and the build breaks. Merget finds these conflicts in meaning before the changes land. See a worked example.

Is there a tool that automatically resolves merge conflicts between pull requests?

Yes. Merget resolves conflicts between open pull requests inside the merge queue. Known conflict shapes are resolved deterministically, harder cases go to a coding agent, and every resolution is checked before it is used. See the conflict resolution benchmark.

Does Merget work with stacked pull requests?

Yes. Stacked pull requests work without a stacking tool, a label or a command, at any depth. In Queue and Autonomous modes Merget retargets the pull requests above one that lands. See how it works.

Which coding agents and languages does Merget support?

Merget works with GitHub pull requests from any agent. The plugin covers Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Devin, Kiro and Google Antigravity, and other clients connect through the MCP server. Code analysis supports C, C#, Go, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, Python, Rust, Scala and TypeScript. See coverage and agent setup.

Can I start without letting Merget change my code?

Yes. Every repository starts read-only, in a mode called Advisory: Merget reports the conflicts it finds without changing source code or merging anything. You choose when it may resolve conflicts, and when it may land work. See the three modes.

Will it respect our reviews and CI?

Yes. Merget lands through your required checks and reviews and revalidates the target before landing. Overrides are separate, deliberate controls for authorized users. Read about access and controls.

What access does the GitHub App need?

The App reads the repositories you select and has write permissions for checks, pull requests, contents and administration. Additional Actions and Workflows permissions enable specific workflows. Advisory limits what Merget does, not the installation’s permission scope. Review the full permissions.

Where does our code go?

Advisory makes no model requests. When Merget resolves conflicts, in Queue and Autonomous modes, conflict context and code a repair agent reads can be sent to a model service. In every mode, Merget may also train its own models on your code, after removing people's names and the credentials it finds. Review the data flow.

What does Merget cost?

The Free plan includes 5,000 credits per month. Team is $50 per month with 10,000 credits and no per-seat charge. Billing remains inactive for organizations in preview. See plans, overage and spending caps.

How do I get started?

Sign up, install the GitHub App on one repository and read the conflicts Merget finds. It changes no code until you turn that on. To talk through your agents and merge workflow first, book a call.

content_html_zh:
Every merge into main multiplies your dev team’s workload.

Each pull request that lands moves main. Every open PR behind it can now conflict or fail CI, and each one is rebased, resolved and rechecked on its own, then again after the next merge.

Git can’t see every conflict.

One pull request renames a function. Another adds a call to its old name. Git merges both cleanly. Every branch passes alone. Main doesn’t.

Every PR wastes tokens and hours across your fleet of agents.

Each agent resolves the same conflicts and CI failures on its own branch. The more pull requests are open, the more of that work is repeated.

1 / 3

PRs from different agents conflict twice as often as PRs from the same agent.

In a replay study, cross-agent pull request pairs hit textual conflicts at about twice the rate of same-agent pairs. Those are only the conflicts Git can see.

Merget reads the code under every open PR, plans the queue and resolves the conflicts in parallel.

01 / Code graph

Read the code under every open PR.

Deep static analysis maps where each name is defined and who calls it across open pull requests. These connections form the foundation for finding conflicts, planning the queue and resolving them.

02 / Data and control flow

Find the conflicts Git misses.

Data and control flow reveal how changes in one pull request affect another. Merget uses that map to detect semantic conflicts that Git merges cleanly, alongside the textual conflicts Git reports.

03 / PR graph

Plan the queue. Resolve in parallel.

The PR graph shows which pull requests can land together and which must go in order. Merget resolves their conflicts in parallel: known shapes directly, and harder cases with coding agents. Every fix lands through your required checks and reviews.

Worktrees keep your agents apart. Merget resolves what collides when they merge.

Worktrees stop agents overwriting each other while they work, but their pull requests still conflict at merge time. GitHub’s merge queue removes a conflicting pull request for you to fix. Merget resolves it in queue order, with the pull requests ahead in view. What it cannot resolve safely comes back to a person.

Once their pull requests conflict, someone has to resolve them.

Compare GitHub merge queue alternatives

Merge queues, merge conflicts and coding agents.

What is Merget?

Merget is a semantic merge queue for GitHub, built for teams running AI coding agents in parallel. It finds conflicts between open pull requests, resolves them in queue order, and lands the result through your required checks and reviews. See how it works.

What is a semantic merge queue?

A semantic merge queue is a merge queue that finds and resolves conflicts in what code means, not only in its text, before pull requests land. For example, one pull request renames a function while another adds a call to its old name. Read the definition and example.

Does GitHub’s merge queue resolve merge conflicts?

No. GitHub’s merge queue removes a pull request that conflicts with the base branch or fails required checks, and the author fixes it and queues again. Merget works on the conflict in queue order instead. How GitHub’s merge queue works.

Do I need GitHub’s merge queue to use Merget?

No. Merget runs its own queue and manages its own landing order. No label, comment or enqueue command is needed, and branch protection is optional. It works with public and private repositories on GitHub.com, for organizations and personal accounts. Read the setup guide.

What are some alternatives to GitHub’s merge queue?

Merget, Mergify, Graphite, Trunk and Aviator are alternatives to GitHub’s merge queue. They differ most in what happens when pull requests conflict: Merget resolves the conflict in queue order, where most queues remove the pull request. Compare the alternatives.

How do I stop merge conflicts between parallel Claude Code agents in git worktrees?

Worktrees stop agents from overwriting each other’s files, but their branches still conflict when they merge. Keep each agent’s pull request small, then let a merge queue order and reconcile them: Merget resolves the conflicts between open pull requests in queue order, so no agent rebases by hand. Read the worktree guide.

Why do pull requests pass CI and still break main?

Because each pull request is tested against the main it branched from, not against the pull requests landing beside it. One renames a function while another adds a call to its old name; Git merges both cleanly and the build breaks. Merget finds these conflicts in meaning before the changes land. See a worked example.

Is there a tool that automatically resolves merge conflicts between pull requests?

是的。 Merget resolves conflicts between open pull requests inside the merge queue. Known conflict shapes are resolved deterministically, harder cases go to a coding agent, and every resolution is checked before it is used. See the conflict resolution benchmark.

Does Merget work with stacked pull requests?

是的。 Stacked pull requests work without a stacking tool, a label or a command, at any depth. In Queue and Autonomous modes Merget retargets the pull requests above one that lands. See how it works.

Which coding agents and languages does Merget support?

Merget works with GitHub pull requests from any agent. The plugin covers Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Devin, Kiro and Google Antigravity, and other clients connect through the MCP server. Code analysis supports C, C#, Go, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, Python, Rust, Scala and TypeScript. See coverage and agent setup.

Can I start without letting Merget change my code?

是的。 Every repository starts read-only, in a mode called Advisory: Merget reports the conflicts it finds without changing source code or merging anything. You choose when it may resolve conflicts, and when it may land work. See the three modes.

Will it respect our reviews and CI?

是的。 Merget lands through your required checks and reviews and revalidates the target before landing. Overrides are separate, deliberate controls for authorized users. Read about access and controls.

What access does the GitHub App need?

The App reads the repositories you select and has write permissions for checks, pull requests, contents and administration. Additional Actions and Workflows permissions enable specific workflows. Advisory limits what Merget does, not the installation’s permission scope. Review the full permissions.

Where does our code go?

Advisory makes no model requests. When Merget resolves conflicts, in Queue and Autonomous modes, conflict context and code a repair agent reads can be sent to a model service. In every mode, Merget may also train its own models on your code, after removing people's names and the credentials it finds. Review the data flow.

What does Merget cost?

The Free plan includes 5,000 credits per month. Team is $50 per month with 10,000 credits and no per-seat charge. Billing remains inactive for organizations in preview. See plans, overage and spending caps.

Sign up, install the GitHub App on one repository and read the conflicts Merget finds. It changes no code until you turn that on. To talk through your agents and merge workflow first, book a call.
